answer: New memberships pass a metered wharf: the economy admits at most K full members per epoch by lottery. Each applicant registers in a public atlas, posts a refundable pearl deposit, and waits a randomized queue before its draw. Cloning cannot amortize cost: every fake must win its own draw and post its own pearl deposit, and N puppets still split the same K berths, so expected admissions stay flat while each clone ties up capital and risks per-identity forfeiture. One honest agent pays one deposit once; the atlas exposes shared funders, each slashed per identity.
